subject: OrbitAI POC: sync on hands-on schedule & fallback matrix
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Park <lauren@orbitai.com>, Chris Thomas <cthomas@orbitai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: OrbitAI POC: sync on hands-on schedule & fallback matrix

Hi Lauren / Chris —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Per our conversation, we'd like to schedule the POC kickoff + a hands-on working session where we can:
- walk through your prompt set and expected success metrics
- pick model candidates for each route and discussion of quantization/latency tradeoffs
- align on routing/fallback rules (region-aware tiering, fallback model hierarchy)
- run a short load test window and confirm monitoring hooks

Proposed slots (PST):
- Wed 18 Feb, 10:00–12:00 (working session + load test prep)
- Thu 19 Feb, 09:00–11:00 (alternate)
- Fri 20 Feb, 13:00–15:00 (if you need east-coast friendly times)

Agenda (attached: POC-Agenda-v1.pdf) — please review before the session. I've also attached a sample prompt set to start (sample-prompt-set.csv). Practical asks from your side:
- Share expected QPS and peak concurrency for the load tests
- Flag any environments/regions you must keep traffic in (eg us-west, us-east)

I'll coordinate internal resources (Marcus for runtime config, Grace for observability, Monica for CS/rollout plan). If the legal/IT folks need to join for SOC2/data questions early, let me know and we'll loop them in.

Next steps: pick one slot and confirm who from OrbitAI will own prework.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: POC-Agenda-v1.pdf, sample-prompt-set.csv
From: Lauren Park <lauren@orbitai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Chris Thomas <cthomas@orbitai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OrbitAI POC: sync on hands-on schedule & fallback matrix

Thanks Naomi — this looks good. We can do Thu 19 Feb 09:00–11:00 PST.

A few notes from our side:
- I'll invite our platform lead (IT) and our security manager to the kickoff — they may only attend the first 30 minutes for the SOC2/data handling discussion.
- For the load test, target traffic: 200 concurrent sessions, burst to 500 qps for short bursts. We'll confirm exact numbers by EOD Friday.
- Can you share a short runbook for the load test (what you'll measure, how to halt, sample payload sizes)? If you have a checklist, that will help our infra team sign off.

Lauren Park
Head of Product, OrbitAI
lauren@orbitai.com | +1 (617) 555-2233

Subject: Re: OrbitAI POC: sync on hands-on schedule & fallback matrix

Naomi / team —

Confirmed from infra side: Thu 19 Feb 09:00–11:00 PST works for our engineers. We'll reserve a staging cluster in us-west with the following shortlist pre-installed for the session:
- redwood/gpt-medium-2025 (float16) — low-latency candidate
- redwood/opt-quant-qa (8-bit) — cost-efficient fallback
- redwood/bert-lite (embedding route) — for reranking tests

Notes / asks:
- For failover tiers, proposing primary->secondary->fallback sequence per route (primary: medium FP16, secondary: quantized 8-bit, fallback: smaller architecture). We should predefine latency windows for automatic fallback at 200ms, 350ms, and 500ms respectively.
- Grace will add observability hooks (token-level latency, per-route error rates). Monica, please draft the customer-facing rollback/incident steps for the load test.

I'll attach a brief draft runbook to the calendar invite, but Naomi, can you also push the loadtest runbook draft (loadtest-runbook-draft.md) to the Drive folder?

—Marcus
